Subject: Priv infra safety & deconflict: IaC module review and risk log

Hi team —

Following up from last week's architecture jam: Acme is ready to move into a private deployment PoC and they've shared a draft repo for the VPC-onprem conversion. I attached an initial risk log (iac-risk-log.xlsx) and the latest network diagram (network-diagram-v2.png). The immediate ask from Acme: validate our Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules for the VPC footprint, routing constraints to their on-prem transit, and CI gating that will drive approvals.

Key constraints from Acme:
- No public egress from model-serving subnets (mandatory egress proxy)
- Private certificate provisioning via their internal ACME CA, certs delivered through a secure artifact bucket
- Audit logs retained for 365 days in an encrypted S3 bucket under their account

What I need from us this week:
1) A short risk synthesis for each IaC module (network, bastion, subnets, nat/egress, tf-state) — see the attached sheet.
2) A proposed CI gating checklist (static analysis, tfsec, helmtemplate unit checks, Ansible idempotence check).
3) Any obvious incompatibilities with their transit gateways (they use Juniper SRX, BGP with MD5).

I've opened a PR with the proposed module diffs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/342 (tf changes in tf-module-diff.patch). Can you review and add line items to the risk log by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks — happy to synthesize and send to Acme once we have consolidated items.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Nov 8, 2026 at 08:23 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following up from last week's architecture jam: Acme is ready to move into a private deployment PoC...

Thanks Marcus — quick first-pass notes inline and action items below. I pulled the repo and skimmed the TF modules and Helm charts. High level: we have a strong starting point but there are a few non-trivial risks that need explicit mitigations before we hand the package to Acme for staging.

Primary concerns (short):
- tf-state access model: current backend assumes Redwood-managed S3/GCS. For Acme we need to support remote state with customer-owned S3 bucket + KMS key (and explicit IAM role assumption). Risk: state exposure across accounts if IAM roles are misconfigured. Mitigation: add role assumption test in CI, and a terraform plan sanitizer check.

- Network egress model: The terraform module for nat-gateway currently leaves an option for public NAT. Since Acme requires no public egress from serving subnets, we need to default to enforced egress-proxy + explicit deny rules. Also ensure helm chart has environment variables to force outbound proxy and fail open/closed behavior documented.

- Certificate provisioning: The Helm chart expects cert-manager issuing a public CA. Need to add a path for their ACME CA via vault or S3-distributed certs. Include a documented bootstrap step and Ansible play to write certs to the nodes.

- BGP + transit compatibility: Juniper SRX MD5 with 4-byte ASN was flagged in the PR notes. Our neighbor config generator needs an option to specify MD5 and BGP timers; test scaffolding should run bgp-open tests in the CI matrix.

- Helm values & secrets: secrets are templated with sealed-secrets by default; for on-prem we should support SOPS + KMS envelope for customers. Document keyflow.

Suggested action split (so reviewers have clear chunks):
- Network (Vanessa): validate subnets, route tables, NACLs, egress proxy; produce a short list of required terraform variable changes.
- State & IAM (Rishi): build the role-assume test and plan sanitizer, verify cross-account KMS policy examples.
- Certificate + Helm (me): add support paths for ACME CA + Ansible bootstrap to copy certs; update helm values to include proxy enforcement.

I will drop line items into the attached iac-risk-log.xlsx and add examples in the PR. If Acme can provide their BGP neighbor exports and an S3 bucket ARN for testing, we can run the network dry-run next week.

Irene Choi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus & Irene — this level of granularity is great. A few notes from our security and procurement team after a quick scan:

- We'll provide the S3 bucket ARN and a service account for role-assume testing by Tuesday (we need to clear it with infra ops).
- Certificate delivery: our CA team prefers certs be pushed to an internal artifact bucket and rotated via a lifecycle policy. Can you add rotation guidance and the Ansible flow for renewals?
- Audit logs: 365 day retention is a hard requirement. Can you confirm that logs from the serving runtime, NLB/ELB equivalents, and host OS syslog will be consolidated into the same encrypted bucket? What encryption key will be used (ours or Redwood-managed)?
- Timeline: procurement wants a one-page note on gating steps and a security owner for each gating item to sign off before we allow PII-adjacent datasets in the PoC.

I attached our security checklist to the thread (we'll upload the formal PDF via procurement). For now please add the owner names in your risk log so our procurement team knows who to contact.

Regards,
Alejandra Gomez
Head of Cloud Engineering
Acme Fintech

- Remote state + KMS + role-assume tests (Rishi) — due Wed EOD: add example customer S3 backend and a CI job that runs assume-role -> terraform plan check.
